summary: Implementation-ready design for #4343 Layer 3 admission control: per-node concurrency cap (refuse a hot node), interactive lane (reserve a stream for cockpit chat + engine plan), and a shared warm-load-aware cluster-slot helper

cap.summary: P1a per-node concurrency CAP design. The only existing balancer (capacity-weighted ORDER BY at department_dispatcher.py:2166-2184 and the preferred_node loop at :5645-5715) SPREADS but never REFUSES a saturated node, so a WTF gemma3:12b batch surge fills USS-246's 3 GPU streams and the engine's interactive 'code' plan still selects it and queues behind 250s jobs. Fix: add a live in-flight count per node (from bridge_jobs WHERE status='running', the authoritative real-time signal — current_load is only heartbeat-derived and lags) and SKIP any candidate whose in-flight >= remote_nodes.max_concurrent during selection, as a PREFERENCE with strict fall-through (next GPU → hub → stationed node → normal flow → never error/drop). Implemented as a CTE join in the assignment query, a guard in the preferred_node loop, and a load-aware refusal in fleet_resource_router.should_dispatch_to_node. Keep FLEET_RESOURCE_ROUTING_ENABLED default OFF for the router enforce-path; gate the new cap behind its own default-ON flag so it can be killed without a deploy.
cap.current_behavior:
Two node-selection sites both pick a saturated node:
1) `_get_node_assignment_for_agent` (department_dispatcher.py:2144-2265). The query (lines 2188-2235) JOINs a 5-min `task_execution_log` COUNT (`load_5m`, lines 2199-2205) and ORDER BYs by capacity-weighted load `COALESCE(load_5m.task_count,0)::float / GREATEST(rn.max_concurrent,1)` (lines 2168, 2182). This only SPREADS — `LIMIT 1` still returns the least-loaded node even if it is at 100% (no WHERE filter on load vs max_concurrent). The 5-min COUNT also lags and undercounts warm sync dispatches.
2) The preferred_node loop (department_dispatcher.py:5645-5730). For each candidate (e.g. CAPABILITY_NODE_AFFINITY `_GPU_CLUSTER` = ['starship_76583490e36955ab','starship_5501c2766526e746'], lines 405-420), it resolves the node by name/id (5658-5664, only checks online+heartbeat — NO load check), builds info via `_get_fleet_node_for_dispatch` (2267-2314, also no load check), and dispatches via `_dispatch_to_node` (2316+). First node that is online wins regardless of in-flight load.
3) `_dispatch_to_node` capacity precheck (2340-2413) calls `should_dispatch_to_node` (fleet_resource_router.py:441-463), which is load-INDEPENDENT: `score_node_for_model` (line 458) only checks memory fit, returns None only on capacity-mismatch; load (`current_load/max_concurrent`, fleet_resource_router.py:182-184) is folded into the rank SCORE, never an admission gate. Enforce path is OFF by default (FLEET_RESOURCE_ROUTING_ENABLED, line 2345).
Live-verified: bridge_jobs WHERE status='running' is the real-time signal — created at dispatch start (2432, status='running', metadata.node_id+node_name), flipped completed (2523) / failed (2589). BUT metadata->>'node_id' is stored as EITHER int DB id ("115", from _get_node_assignment_for_agent:2259 = rn.id) OR varchar node_id ("starship_76583490e36955ab", from _get_fleet_node_for_dispatch:2308 = rn.node_id) — same node, both forms live right now. remote_nodes.current_load is hub-derived in heartbeat (fleet_node_routes.py:2587 comment) — lags, do NOT use for admission.
cap.fallback_behavior:
Strictly preference-with-fallback; a dispatch is NEVER dropped or errored:
1) Assignment query: the new in-flight CTE is a LEFT JOIN; the cap is applied as an ORDER-BY DEMOTION (saturated nodes sort LAST), NOT a hard WHERE — so even if EVERY eligible node is at/over cap the query still returns the least-over-cap one (LIMIT 1 always yields a row when any node exists). This guarantees no NULL-return regression that would block stationed agents.
2) preferred_node loop: a candidate over its cap is SKIPPED (`continue`) exactly like the existing 'not viable' path (5716-5720) — falls to the next candidate (next GPU → hub if in list), then after the loop falls through to the normal flow (5727+), then hub, then the agent's stationed node, then cloud. If ALL preferred candidates are capped, the block is a no-op and normal routing proceeds.
3) should_dispatch_to_node load refusal: returns allowed=False ONLY when enforce=True AND in-flight>=max_concurrent; with the existing FLEET_RESOURCE_ROUTING_ENABLED default OFF this is soft-warn (logs reason, allows) — so it cannot strand work. When _dispatch_to_node gets None back (2398) the caller already escalates to the next tier.
4) New cap gated by platform_settings `dispatch:node_cap:enabled` (default ON) read via a TTL-cached helper; flip to off = instant revert to today's behavior with no deploy. Any exception in the cap path is caught and treated as 'not capped' (fail-open), mirroring the capacity-precheck fail-open at 2411-2413.
The cap is a PREFERENCE: at-cap nodes are deprioritized, never permanently refused, so a sole capable node for a model still serves (escalation always has the hub as the universal-capable fallback).
cap.key_sql_or_signature:
-- AUTHORITATIVE real-time in-flight count per node id, resolving BOTH metadata node_id forms
-- (int DB id "115" AND varchar node_id "starship_...") to remote_nodes.id.
-- Drop-in CTE for _get_node_assignment_for_agent (replaces/augments the load_5m subquery):
WITH inflight AS (
  SELECT rn.id AS node_id, COUNT(bj.id) AS running
  FROM remote_nodes rn
  LEFT JOIN bridge_jobs bj
    ON bj.status = 'running'
   AND ( bj.metadata->>'node_id' = rn.node_id          -- varchar form
      OR bj.metadata->>'node_id' = rn.id::text )         -- int-DB-id form
  GROUP BY rn.id
)
-- join: LEFT JOIN inflight ON inflight.node_id = rn.id
-- ORDER BY: demote saturated nodes FIRST, then existing capacity-weighted spread:
--   (CASE WHEN COALESCE(inflight.running,0) >= GREATEST(rn.max_concurrent,1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ASC,
--   <existing order_by terms unchanged>
-- (Keep the existing fleet-first / news / hub branches; prepend the cap term to each.)

plan_steps.change: In _get_node_assignment_for_agent, add an `inflight` CTE (LEFT JOIN bridge_jobs status='running' resolving BOTH metadata->>'node_id' = rn.node_id (varchar) AND = rn.id::text (int form), GROUP BY rn.id) and LEFT JOIN it to the main query. Prepend a saturation-demotion term to EACH order_by branch (lines 2161-2184): `(CASE WHEN COALESCE(inflight.running,0) >= GREATEST(rn.max_concurrent,1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ASC, ...existing...`. Keep load_5m as the secondary spread tiebreak. Gate behind `self._node_cap_enabled()` — when off, emit the original order_by unchanged.
plan_steps.rationale: Demotes (not deletes) saturated nodes at the primary selection site so a full USS-246 yields to the next GPU/hub, while LIMIT 1 still always returns a row (no NULL-return regression). bridge_jobs is the real-time signal; current_load lags. Resolving both id forms is mandatory (live-verified both exist).

plan_steps.change: Add two module/instance helpers near _node_circuit_open: `_node_inflight_count(node_db_id:int)->int` (COUNT bridge_jobs status='running' matching both metadata node_id forms; fail-open 0) and `_node_over_cap(node_db_id,max_concurrent)->bool`. Also add `_node_cap_enabled()->bool` reading platform_settings 'dispatch:node_cap:enabled' (default true) with a short TTL cache, mirroring existing _is_*_enabled helpers.
plan_steps.rationale: Single source of the in-flight truth reused by both selection sites and the router precheck; cap is killable without deploy.

plan_steps.change: In the preferred_node loop, after resolving `_pn_db_id` (5666) and before building info, when `_node_cap_enabled()`: fetch the node's max_concurrent in the same SELECT (add max_concurrent column at 5659) and `if self._node_over_cap(_pn_db_id, _pn_max_concurrent): log 'preferred_node %s saturated — trying next'; continue`. This reuses the existing 'not viable → next candidate → fall through to hub' path (5716-5730).
plan_steps.rationale: Closes the interactive-starvation gap directly: a saturated affinity GPU node is passed over to the next GPU then hub, so the engine 'code' plan never queues behind a full USS-246. Strict fall-through preserves fail-safe.

plan_steps.change: Extend should_dispatch_to_node with an optional `inflight:int|None=None` param. After the existing score-None capacity check, add a load gate: max_conc=GREATEST(max_concurrent,1); load = inflight if provided else current_load; if load>=max_conc return (not enforce, 'node-saturated: inflight=X>=max_concurrent=Y'). Soft-warn when enforce=False (logs, allows).
plan_steps.rationale: Makes the router load-AWARE (today it is capacity-only) without forcing it on. Defense-in-depth third gate; behavior unchanged while FLEET_RESOURCE_ROUTING_ENABLED stays off.

plan_steps.change: At the should_dispatch_to_node call site, pass `inflight=self._node_inflight_count(int_node_id)` (node_id is already normalized to int at 2362-2365). Leave the existing 'capacity-mismatch' hard-refuse (2399-2409) untouched; the new saturation reason is soft unless enforce=True.
plan_steps.rationale: Wires the live count into the precheck so enabling FLEET_RESOURCE_ROUTING_ENABLED later gives a real per-node load refusal, not just memory-fit.

plan_steps.change: OPTIONAL (low priority, separate commit): allow score_node_for_model to accept a live inflight override for the load-pressure term (line 183 cur_load) so the RANK also reflects real-time load, not just heartbeat current_load. Default unchanged (reads current_load) to avoid extra queries in the hot ranking loop.
plan_steps.rationale: Improves find_best_node_for_model ranking accuracy; deferred because it adds a per-node query inside a scoring loop — keep P1a minimal.

plan_steps.change: Add idempotent seed: INSERT INTO platform_settings(key,value) VALUES ('dispatch:node_cap:enabled','true') ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. No schema change needed (idx_bridge_jobs_status + idx_bridge_jobs_metadata_gin already exist, so the in-flight count is index-supported).
plan_steps.rationale: Provides the no-deploy kill switch; existing indexes keep the count query cheap on the hot path.

risks: bridge_jobs.metadata->>'node_id' is stored in TWO forms (int '115' AND varchar 'starship_...') for the same node — verified live. If the count SQL matches only one form it UNDERCOUNTS by ~half and the cap silently under-fires. Mitigation: match both (rn.node_id OR rn.id::text) in every count site.

Stale 'running' rows: if a fleet dispatch crashes without flipping status (e.g. process kill), a phantom running row inflates the count and could over-demote a healthy node. Mitigation: the cap is a demotion not a hard block (LIMIT 1 still returns a node); also dispatch_zombie_reaper already reaps stale running jobs. Optionally bound the count to created_at > NOW()-INTERVAL '20 minutes' to ignore zombies.

Per-dispatch extra query in the hot path: _node_inflight_count adds 1 COUNT per preferred_node candidate and per _dispatch_to_node call. Mitigation: idx_bridge_jobs_status + GIN index make it cheap; the assignment-query CTE is a single GROUP BY, not N queries. Keep the helper short-circuited when _node_cap_enabled() is false.

Demotion term changes ORDER BY → could shift routing for non-saturated cases if mis-written. Mitigation: term is `CASE ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ASC` prepended — for an UNSATURATED fleet every node scores 0 so ordering is byte-for-byte unchanged. Verify with a unit test asserting identical ordering when all inflight=0.

Hot dispatch path: any exception must fail-open. Mitigation: every new helper wraps in try/except returning 0/False; the CTE is a LEFT JOIN (COALESCE 0). Mirror the existing 2411-2413 fail-open pattern.

node_id int-vs-varchar trap (fleet.md HARD RULE): never pass int id to a `WHERE node_id=%s` varchar query. Mitigation: helpers take node_db_id (int) and either join via rn.id or cast rn.id::text — never compare the varchar column to an int.
cap.verification: Live, non-disruptive: (1) Before deploy, run the in-flight CTE as a read-only SELECT against the live DB and compare per-node `running` to `SELECT metadata->>'node_id', metadata->>'node_name', COUNT(*) FROM bridge_jobs WHERE status='running' GROUP BY 1,2` (already run this session) to confirm both id forms resolve to the right node. (2) Unit test in platform_v2/tests: assert _get_node_assignment_for_agent ordering is identical to baseline when all nodes have 0 inflight (no regression), and that a node with inflight>=max_concurrent sorts LAST. (3) After deploy with flag ON: synthetically insert N>max_concurrent fake 'running' bridge_jobs rows tagged to USS-246 (id 115), dispatch a 'code' capability, confirm via task_execution_log/bridge_jobs that it landed on USS-245 or hub, not 115; delete the fake rows. (4) Flag-OFF smoke: set dispatch:node_cap:enabled=false, confirm routing matches pre-change behavior. (5) Monitor logs for 'preferred_node %s saturated — trying next' and 'node-saturated' reasons. Never run failover.sh / touch DNS. Never curl Ollama directly — observe via DB + logs only.

lane.summary: P1b INTERACTIVE LANE design: (1) tag the two interactive callers (cockpit + engine via /api/internal/dhq/chat, and delegate/WTF/backfill batch callers) with explicit priority='high'/'critical' vs 'low'; (2) reserve >=1 stream per GPU fleet node for interactive by parameterizing the P1a per-node cap with an `interactive` flag derived from priority>=high — batch occupies at most max_concurrent-1 streams, leaving an interactive slot free; (3) make priority actually gate the WARM hot path (not just the cold-load queue) via a per-node admission check that runs BEFORE _find_fleet_agent_for_hub_agent / _pick_fleet_node, plus a hub-local interactive bypass so cockpit/engine never queue behind a batch surge. 'interactive' is detected centrally in request_work as `priority in ('high','critical')` (no new flag needed — priority already flows through dispatch()/dispatch_json **kwargs). Concrete edits below.
lane.current_behavior:
PRIORITY FLOW: caller → dispatch() (department_dispatcher.py:9845, **kwargs) / dispatch_json() (:9982) → BridgeDispatcher.request_work(priority='normal' default, :5383) → _PRIORITY_INT={"low":3,"normal":5,"high":7,"critical":9} (:5373). Priority ONLY influences the COLD path: (a) CPU-model queue insert (:6585-6615, priority_int written to dispatch_pending_queue), (b) model_not_ready queue insert (:6691-6744). The WARM synchronous path NEVER reads priority: node routing at _find_fleet_agent_for_hub_agent (:2130-2240, the capacity-weighted ORDER BY at :2162-2184 spreads by 5-min task COUNT/max_concurrent but never refuses), preferred_node loop (:5644-5730), node-preferred warm exec (:5736-5786), score-based _pick_fleet_node (:5790+), and final hub _execute_llm (:6652, :3409). So a busy node still sorts-first-and-wins for an interactive call, and a hub-local interactive chat (local_only=True from dhq/chat) runs a plain synchronous _execute_llm Ollama call (:6652) that contends head-to-head with any concurrent batch hub call — no lane.
CALLER TAGS TODAY: cockpit chat + engine plan BOTH hit POST /api/internal/dhq/chat (app.py:4413-4480) → dispatch(capability=conversation|code, prefer_agent=A.R.C.H.I.E.|F.O.R.G.E., local_only=True) with NO priority kwarg → defaults to 'normal'. Engine reaches this via archie_engine/hub/connector.py:147 dispatch()→call_tool('generate_code') OR the dhq/chat HTTP path (#4256 docstring). Batch callers also untagged or MIS-tagged: WTF bias (jobs.py:2818 capability='bias_analysis', no priority='normal'), WTF fact_check (:3196), WTF geo (:3003), backfill re-dispatch (jobs.py:1632-1638 priority='high' — WRONG, a batch drain tagged high), delegate_task_worker (delegation_service.py:830 dispatch(), no priority). Net: interactive and batch are indistinguishable at the warm path.
LIVE-LOAD GAP (confirms why a cap is needed): task_execution_log has priority,node_used_id,module_source,created_at but is written POST-completion (:3926 INSERT after result) so the :2200 load_5m subquery lags. bridge_jobs has status='running',module_source,agent_name but NO node_used_id and NO priority — so neither table gives a clean live per-node, per-lane in-flight count today.
lane.key_sql_or_signature:
NEW central detection (request_work, add right after priority normalization near :5407): 
  `is_interactive = priority in ("high", "critical")`  # no new param; piggybacks existing priority kwarg

NEW helper for the per-node reserved-slot cap (department_dispatcher.py, near :2130). Live in-flight load measured WITHOUT a lagging COUNT, by combining bridge_jobs(running) for fleet jobs + a short 90s task_execution_log window split by lane. The cap caller passes is_interactive so batch is held to max_concurrent-1:

  def _node_has_free_slot(self, node_id: int, max_concurrent: int, is_interactive: bool) -> bool:
      reserve = 0 if is_interactive else 1          # batch leaves >=1 interactive slot
      effective_cap = max(1, max_concurrent - reserve)
      sql = """
        SELECT COUNT(*) FROM task_execution_log
        WHERE node_used_id = %s
          AND created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '90 seconds'
          AND duration_ms IS NULL            -- in-flight rows (logged at start; see note)
      """
      # in-flight count for this node; admit only if live < effective_cap
      return live_inflight < effective_cap

NOTE — to make duration_ms IS NULL meaningful, add a START-of-dispatch task_execution_log insert (or a lightweight in_flight table) so live load is observable, since today the row is only written at :3926 on completion. Minimal-risk alternative that needs NO schema change: a process-local in-memory per-node semaphore dict keyed by node_id (threading.BoundedSemaphore(max_concurrent), batch acquires with reserve), since all warm dispatch runs in the one gunicorn/dispatcher process — but that misses cross-node fleet load. Recommended: small `node_inflight` UNLOGGED table (node_id, dispatch_uuid, lane, started_at) inserted before _dispatch_to_node/_execute_llm and deleted in finally; cap query counts rows per node_id where lane='batch' is denied a slot when inflight >= max_concurrent-1.

ENGINE/COCKPIT priority injection signatures (app.py:4456 dispatch call) — add:
  priority = "critical" if module_id == "archie_comms" else "high"   # cockpit chat = critical, engine plan = high
  ... dispatch(..., priority=priority)
lane.fallback_behavior:
The interactive lane is STRICTLY fail-safe and never drops a dispatch:
- If _node_has_free_slot returns False for a candidate node, that node is SKIPPED in the node-selection loop (same skip semantics as the existing preferred_node 'not viable — trying next' fall-through at :5731) and routing continues to the next candidate → other fleet node → hub → cloud. A refused node never aborts the dispatch.
- An INTERACTIVE dispatch (is_interactive=True) uses reserve=0, so it can claim the last/reserved stream on any node — it is never refused by the cap; only BATCH is held to max_concurrent-1.
- HUB interactive bypass: for local_only interactive calls that land on the final hub _execute_llm (:6652), the reserved slot is enforced ONLY against batch hub calls; an interactive hub call always proceeds (reserve=0). If the in-flight measurement errors (DB/semaphore failure), the helper returns True (fail-open) so a measurement bug can never starve or block dispatch.
- If ALL fleet nodes refuse a batch call (all at max_concurrent-1), batch falls through to the hub (existing behavior) or, for cold models, to the dispatch_pending_queue where the existing priority_int ordering (already correct) drains it later — batch is delayed, never lost.
- preferred_node explicit pins still win first; the cap only gates the auto/score node-selection so E.T.H.O.S.-style GPU pins are unaffected on a miss (they already fall through).

plan_steps.change: In request_work, immediately after the priority is finalized, compute `is_interactive = priority in ('high','critical')` and thread it into the node-selection helpers. This is the single source of 'interactive' detection — no new param, piggybacks the existing priority kwarg that already flows through dispatch()/dispatch_json().
plan_steps.rationale: Centralizes lane detection so cockpit/engine (tagged high/critical) and batch (low/normal) are distinguishable at the WARM path, which today ignores priority entirely.

plan_steps.change: Add `_node_has_free_slot(self, node_id, max_concurrent, is_interactive)` (signature in key_sql). batch reserve=1 (effective cap max_concurrent-1), interactive reserve=0. Measure LIVE in-flight per node (recommended: small UNLOGGED `node_inflight` table written before _dispatch_to_node/_execute_llm, deleted in finally; fallback fail-open=True on any error).
plan_steps.rationale: P1a gives the per-node cap; P1b parameterizes it by lane so batch can never occupy the last stream — guaranteeing a free interactive slot per GPU node. Live measurement fixes the lagging 5-min COUNT gap (task_execution_log is post-hoc; bridge_jobs lacks node_used_id).

plan_steps.change: In _find_fleet_agent_for_hub_agent, after SELECT returns the ranked candidate node(s), gate the chosen node through `_node_has_free_slot(node_id, max_concurrent, is_interactive)`; if it returns False (batch hitting a full-minus-reserve node), continue to the next ranked node (change LIMIT 1 → fetch a small ranked set and pick the first admissible). Pass is_interactive in via an instance attr set in request_work or a new kwarg.
plan_steps.rationale: Makes the spread-only ORDER BY actually REFUSE an over-loaded node for batch, while letting interactive take the reserved slot. This is the warm-path enforcement the cold queue already has.

plan_steps.change: In the preferred_node loop and the score-based _pick_fleet_node block (~5790), apply the same `_node_has_free_slot` gate for batch lane only; on refusal, fall to the next candidate (reuse existing 'trying next'/fall-through). Interactive (reserve=0) is never refused here.
plan_steps.rationale: All four warm routing entry points (node_agents, preferred_node, score-based, hub) must honor the lane or batch leaks through an ungated path.

plan_steps.change: Before the final hub _execute_llm fallthrough, if NOT is_interactive, gate hub batch execution through a hub reserved-slot check (hub max_concurrent=5 → batch capped at 4 concurrent hub streams). Interactive (cockpit local_only chat / engine plan) ALWAYS proceeds. Wrap the in-flight insert/delete around _execute_llm in try/finally.
plan_steps.rationale: The cockpit's local_only=True chat lands here and contends head-to-head with batch hub calls today (the 18-dispatch / 250s symptom). Reserving a hub stream for interactive is the core starvation fix on the hub itself.

plan_steps.change: In api_internal_dhq_chat, set `priority = 'critical' if module_id == 'archie_comms' else 'high'` and pass `priority=priority` to dispatch(). Cockpit (module_id='archie_comms') = critical; engine plan (module_id='archie_code_engine') = high.
plan_steps.rationale: Tags BOTH interactive callers at the source so the central detection lights up. critical>high so a human at the cockpit outranks even the engine's plan step.

plan_steps.change: Add `priority='low'` to the delegate_task_worker dispatch() call.
plan_steps.rationale: delegate_task_worker is pure batch drain; tagging low keeps it out of the reserved interactive slot.

plan_steps.change: Add `priority='low'` to the WTF bias_analysis (:2818), fact_check (:3196), geo_extraction (:3003), and *_backlog (:3479,:3614,:3796) dispatch() calls.
plan_steps.rationale: These are the gemma3:12b/7B batch surge that starved the engine; tagging low forces them to leave the per-node interactive slot free.

plan_steps.change: Change the backfill re-dispatch priority from 'high' to 'low' (currently MIS-tagged high at :1638).
plan_steps.rationale: The stuck-queue backfill worker is a background drain, not interactive — tagging it 'high' would let a batch reclaim the reserved interactive slot. Correct it to 'low'.

plan_steps.change: OPTIONAL: add a `welfare:lane:batch_reserve` platform_setting (default 1) read by _node_has_free_slot so the reserved-slot count is tunable without deploy (mirrors existing welfare:break:* / welfare:backlog:* pattern).
plan_steps.rationale: Lets ops widen the interactive reserve (e.g. 2) on a saturated cluster without a code change, consistent with the existing tunable-threshold convention.

risks: Live in-flight measurement: task_execution_log is written post-completion (:3926) and bridge_jobs lacks node_used_id+priority, so an accurate live per-node lane count needs a NEW write (UNLOGGED node_inflight table OR a start-of-dispatch log insert). If skipped, the cap falls back to the lagging 5-min COUNT and the reservation is approximate. Mitigation: fail-open (return True) on any measurement error so dispatch is never blocked.

Hot path latency: _node_has_free_slot adds a DB round-trip per node candidate on the synchronous dispatch path. Mitigation: single indexed query (idx_task_execution_log_node_used exists) or in-memory semaphore; cache per request.

Over-reservation on a 1-stream node: Starship-245 max_concurrent=1 → batch reserve=1 leaves 0 batch slots, effectively making .245 interactive-only. May be desirable, but verify it doesn't strand all .245 batch capacity. Mitigation: clamp effective_cap=max(1, ...) already does this — a 1-stream node still serves batch when no interactive is in flight only if reserve logic checks live interactive presence rather than static subtraction (consider: reserve only when an interactive call is actually waiting).

engine path duality: engine reaches dispatch via BOTH connector.call_tool('generate_code') AND the dhq/chat HTTP route — only the dhq/chat path gets the app.py priority tag. Verify which path the plan step actually uses (#4256) or tag generate_code's dispatch too, else the engine plan stays 'normal'.

prefer_agent lock interaction: a batch call with job_id auto-locks an agent (:5407 region) — if that agent is interactive-tier's home agent (A.R.C.H.I.E./F.O.R.G.E.), batch could still occupy the agent. Lane reservation is per-NODE-stream, not per-agent, so this is mostly orthogonal, but confirm A.R.C.H.I.E.'s warm model isn't single-instance-locked by a batch job.

critical priority side-effect: priority='critical' currently also bypasses the CPU-model queue (:6585) and model_not_ready queue (:6691). Two disjoint dispatch paths, neither globally load-aware:

  def get_cluster_slots(cur=None) -> dict:

  def should_admit_batch(target_model: str | None = None, *, want: int = 1, gpu_bound: bool | None = None, cur=None) -> tuple[bool, int, dict]:
      '''Returns (admit, recommended_workers, slots_dict).

         admit=False when the relevant free pool (gpu_free if gpu_bound else cluster_free) <= the matching headroom.
         recommended_workers = max(0, free_pool - headroom) clamped to [0, want].'''

  def assert_cluster_invariants(cur=None) -> list[str]:  # drift guard, returns list of warnings (empty=ok)

Core SQL (validated live — returns total_slots=39, GPU subcluster .246=3/.245=1, hub warm=3):
  WITH nodes AS (
    SELECT id, node_id, node_name, max_concurrent
    FROM remote_nodes WHERE status='online' AND approval_status='approved'),
  warm AS (
    SELECT node_used_id AS nid, COUNT(*) n FROM task_execution_log
    WHERE created_at > NOW() - (%(win)s||' seconds')::interval AND node_used_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY node_used_id),
  cold AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(result_node_id, preferred_node_id, node_preference) AS nid, COUNT(*) n
    FROM dispatch_pending_queue WHERE status IN ('queued','running')
    GROUP BY COALESCE(result_node_id, preferred_node_id, node_preference))
  SELECT n.node_id, n.id AS db_id, n.node_name, n.max_concurrent,
         COALESCE(w.n,0) warm, COALESCE(c.n,0) cold,
         GREATEST(0, n.max_concurrent - COALESCE(w.n,0) - COALESCE(c.n,0)) free
  FROM nodes n LEFT JOIN warm w ON w.nid=n.id LEFT JOIN cold c ON c.nid=n.id;

slots.fallback_behavior:
Helper is advisory + fail-open at every layer so it can NEVER drop or block a dispatch path:
- get_cluster_slots/should_admit_batch wrap all DB work in try/except; on ANY error they return a permissive default (cluster_free = a large number, admit=True, recommended_workers=want) — identical safety posture to the current _wtf_cluster_slots `return 4,0,{}` and _wtf_backlog_pool_over_budget `return False`.
- It governs only BATCH PRODUCERS (the should_admit_batch / recommended_workers callers). It does NOT touch department_dispatcher.request_work, _get_node_assignment_for_agent, the preferred_node loop, or model_dispatch_worker — so interactive/cockpit/engine dispatches and the existing capacity-weighted ORDER BY node selection are completely unchanged. Reserving headroom means batches admit FEWER workers, never fewer than 0; when full they defer to the next scheduled cycle (the existing 'break/return — retry next cycle' behavior in every WTF caller), exactly like today's per-model queued>10 gate.
- _wtf_cluster_slots shim preserves the exact (_workers,_qdepth,_by_model) return contract and the by_model['model']['queued'] shape the 5 callers index, and keeps the 'min(2 if >40 else 4)' clamp — so the per-model cold gates (jobs.py:2909,3082,3405,3703,3876) keep functioning. No caller signature changes.
- Drift guard assert_cluster_invariants only LOGS warnings (returns a list) — it never raises into the hot path. It is called once per cycle from the cheapest producer (e.g. a 5-min observer) and emits a system_notification on drift, never gating dispatch.
- If platform_settings rows are missing, the module-level INTERACTIVE_HEADROOM/GPU_INTERACTIVE_HEADROOM/WARM_WINDOW_SECONDS constants are the defaults (merge_break_config-style read).
risks: WARM PROXY IS LAGGING, NOT EXACT: task_execution_log has no in-flight/completed_at marker (verified — only created_at on completion), so warm_recent counts COMPLETED rows in the last WARM_WINDOW_SECONDS, which over-counts a node that just finished short tasks and under-counts a single long-running warm dispatch (e.g. a 250s gemma3:12b in-flight produces 0 task_execution_log rows until it finishes). This is the SAME inherent limitation the existing 5-min COUNT load-balancer has; 90s narrows it. The only exact fix would be an in-flight marker (out of P1c scope) — note it for a P2 follow-up.

NODE ATTRIBUTION OF QUEUED COLD ROWS: live dispatch_pending_queue queued rows currently have result_node_id/preferred_node_id/node_preference all NULL (verified — 104 queued, all NULL nid), so cold queued work attributes to no node and is only counted cluster-wide, not per-node. Acceptable for admission (cluster_free still reflects it) but per-node cold counts undercount until the queue carries a node hint; flag as a known limitation.

GPU-BOUND INFERENCE BY MODEL NAME is heuristic (a model list). If a new heavy model is added to CAPABILITY_NODE_AFFINITY without updating cluster_slots' GPU-model set, its batches will be admitted against the 39-slot cluster pool instead of the 4-slot GPU pool. The drift guard should also assert the GPU-model set ⊇ models implied by CAPABILITY_NODE_AFFINITY capabilities to catch this.

HEADROOM TUNING: INTERACTIVE_HEADROOM=1 cluster-wide is tiny vs 39 slots; the real contention is the GPU subcluster (4 slots) where GPU_INTERACTIVE_HEADROOM=1 leaves only 3 for batches. Verify this doesn't over-throttle WTF on quiet days; expose both via platform_settings for live tuning without deploy.

IMPORT COUPLING: cluster_slots importing dispatcher._GPU_CLUSTER creates a dept_hq->services edge; safer to define GPU_CLUSTER_NODE_IDS in cluster_slots and have the drift guard assert equality with dispatcher._GPU_CLUSTER (single source still the dispatcher, validated by the guard) to avoid a circular import on the hot path.
